A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POET research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original C4 pretraining experiments, BART summarization results, ablations, and training-dynamics analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds 3B-model pretraining, GLUE evaluations, and spectral-entropy and hyperspherical-energy comparisons.

M1.justification: POET's two-sided orthogonal reparameterization, initialization schemes, stochastic primitives, Cayley–Neumann approximation, and merge-then-reinitialize procedure remain unchanged. Corrected dimensions for P align the algorithm description with its existing definition; revised truncation settings do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v4 adds eight GLUE tasks covering acceptability, inference, paraphrase, sentiment, and semantic similarity. C4 pretraining and XSum/CNN-DailyMail summarization remain; the latter moves to Appendix L. The 3B experiment expands model scale, not dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Muon becomes an evaluated comparator against AdamW and POET in v4 Figures 6–7; v1 only discussed and cited it. Comparator membership in the retained pretraining and summarization tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 adds a 3B-model run on 5B tokens, GLUE finetuning for 10 epochs at learning rate 2e-5 with task-specific metrics, and spectral-entropy/energy diagnostics. It also revises the reported Neumann sweep from k=1–5 to k=0–4 and recommends k=3, versus v1's main-text recommendation of 5 and appendix setting of 4. These reporting revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: New Llama-60M analyses test whether POET maintains spectral diversity and low hyperspherical energy relative to AdamW and Muon (Figures 6–7). Existing initialization, merge-frequency, vector-probing, update-coverage, and singular-value analyses remain; the Neumann analysis receives revised truncation labels and recommendations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Appendix A's unchanged variance calculation concerns theoretical vector probing, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: v4 adds 3B perplexities of 16.90 for POET-FS and 19.61 for AdamW on 5B tokens, GLUE scores, and spectral/energy trajectories. GLUE generally favors POET pretraining, but Full FT on STS-B scores 0.873 versus AdamW's 0.880. Original Table 2 and relocated summarization scores remain unchanged; Neumann perplexities are retained under shifted k labels.

T1.justification: New Appendix B supplies a Gaussian mean/covariance derivation claiming distribution preservation under RWP and consequently small hyperspherical energy. v1 contained only an informal distribution-preservation assertion in related work. The existing spectrum bounds, stochastic-primitive proofs, and vector-probing derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about spectral preservation, scalable approximations, parameter efficiency, generalization, and applicability to pretraining and finetuning. The added experiments support these existing headline claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations linking spectral diversity to optimization directions and low hyperspherical energy to generalization and Gaussian initialization. It qualifies energy preservation as holding in expectation rather than exactly, and adds interpretations of GLUE transferability and larger-scale performance. Its claim of superiority across every GLUE task overlooks Table 4's STS-B exception.

D1.justification: v4 documents GLUE epochs and learning rate, states that the 3B run reuses 1.3B hyperparameters, and revises Neumann truncation guidance. Existing architecture tables, hardware information, CUDA implementation details, codebase links, and the promise to release code remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Four references are added for SVD analysis, effective rank, Kaiming initialization, and GLUE. Discussion expands the connection to Muon's spectral diversity, while the established positioning relative to orthogonal training, sparse training, low-rank methods, and optimizers remains.

P1.justification: v4 tightens wording in Section 2, introduces a downstream-finetuning subsection, moves BART summarization to Appendix L, adds Appendix B and acknowledgements, and updates the conference header. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds a six-panel spectral-entropy figure, a hyperspherical-energy figure, and dedicated 3B and GLUE tables. It relocates and enlarges the summarization table and revises Neumann plot legends, typography, and some axis ranges. Most earlier figures are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: GLUE now tests transfer of POET-pretrained representations, complementing v1's BART finetuning study, and the 3B experiment strengthens scaling evidence. Neumann recommendations also become more consistent. These gains are limited by the unspecified GLUE model size, the overstated all-task superiority claim, and Appendix B's failure to justify Gaussian invariance when R and P are learned from the initialized weights.
